calibration.method: 54 fixed adapter settings; Texas event only. Reject any alert earlier than 72 h before EEA3, then maximize positive lead within 72 h. Tie-break on fewer alert hours, shorter peak window, smaller generation multiplier. This fits the demonstration event and does not establish predictive accuracy.

meter-time.definition: Every alert episode start in the 2019-2020 control period is counted as an unverified/false alarm. No event labels were supplied; some may coincide with real grid stress. Consecutive alert hours count as one episode; month boundaries do not reset episodes.

public-delay.definition: Every alert episode start in the 2019-2020 control period is counted as an unverified/false alarm. No event labels were supplied; some may coincide with real grid stress. Consecutive alert hours count as one episode; month boundaries do not reset episodes.

timing.meter-time: Ideal immediate BA meter access and prior-day 11 ET access to BA day-ahead DF. Retrospective event-time replay, not public EIA availability.
timing.public-delay: NG withheld until next BA operating day 11 ET; DF until target BA operating day 11 ET. Actions evaluated hourly with actual meter timestamps. Module horizon is 36 h after newest meter, so a delayed meter shortens remaining actionable horizon.

assumptions: One aggregate plant, not individual generators. Raw D is measured load served, not total demand including disconnected customers.

NG is dispatched generation, not available capacity. Tuned plantMeter is an assumed capacity proxy: trailing maximum NG multiplied by a fitted factor; no measured reserves or imports are available in these series.
Critical share=25% is an adapter assumption, changes shed amount but not the alert trigger. Census people=1 is a contract placeholder, not a population estimate.
Demand outlook uses only released day-ahead DF; unavailable targets persist last measured D. No future realized generation or demand enters observations.
Historical EIA data are revised, not original release vintages. Publication schedules are conservative approximations, not exact historical arrival logs.
Texas is the calibration event, not an independent test. Elliott is a transfer check. TVA/DUK imports limit comparisons using NG alone.
Hold-out false alarms are conservative unverified episode starts, without labeled real emergencies. Also inspect alert-hour fractions.
